title: Split lint plugins into workspace-scoped plugins and migrate release hooks to Go adapter
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic lint executor was the source of frequent CI re-runs and slow premerge feedback. It loaded language-specific plugins for every changed package and made the presubmit runner sensitive to unrelated workspace files. This PR separates lint plugins into workspace-scoped plugin bundles so that each presubmit only loads the minimum plugin set required for changed files.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces a workspace-plugin registry (plugins/workspace-manifest.yaml) and a thin loader used by the presubmit runner.
- Moves existing lint adapters into workspace-scoped packages (tools/lint/plugins/*) and converts the TypeScript/Node bootstrap for release hooks into a small Go-based release adapter (tools/release/adapter) for reliability in CI images.
- Adds deterministic plugin activation: changed-file patterns are used to compute the minimal plugin set. This reduces cold-start work in the lint runner and avoids pulling unrelated toolchains into the job container.
- Replaces fragile bash-based release hooks with a Go binary that uses our internal release library (releasekit) to perform signing, changelog stamping, and artifact promotion. The adapter is idempotent and exposes clearer exit codes for the CI orchestrator.
- Adds unit tests and integration smoke tests for the workspace manifest resolver and release adapter.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- The workspace manifest is intentionally small and declarative to avoid coupling the presubmit runner with repo-specific heuristics. A future PR will add a caching layer for monorepo hot paths.
- The Go release adapter reduces flakiness seen on alpine-based CI images where the Node runtime occasionally timed out on large payloads. However, this increases the binary build step in CI; the adapter is cross-compiled and cached in the build matrix.

Checklist:
- [x] Add workspace manifest and plugin bundles
- [x] Wire presubmit runner to compute minimal plugin set
- [x] Implement Go release adapter with tests
- [x] Update devcontainer and CONTRIBUTING.md notes
- [x] Run full CI and fix lint/test fallout

Related work: ENG-3241 (presubmit feedback speed), ENG-3308 (release automation reliability). See internal RFC: https://linear.redwood.ai/ENG-3241 for perf numbers and design notes.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice decomposition. Question: how does the manifest generation work for generated code directories? We should ignore build/ and dist/ by default.
Maya Thompson: Good point — added default excludes for build/, dist/, and third_party/ in the manifest generator (see plugins/workspace-manifest.yaml). Added tests to cover generated dirs.
Leah Park: Can you add an integration-run that exercises the cross-compiled adapter in the same image we use in release pipelines? We had subtle env issues earlier.
Maya Thompson: Added a smoke job to ci/ci-matrix.yml that uses the release adapter image and runs a dry-run promotion. Marked it opt-in to avoid long presubmit runs.
Carlos Mendes: Two nits: document the CLI exit codes and add a small e2e that asserts idempotency on repeated runs.
Maya Thompson: Addressed both nits. exit codes documented in tools/release/adapter/README and e2e added as adapter_test.go::TestAdapterIdempotent
release_notes: Improved presubmit feedback speed by scoping lint plugins to changed workspaces; reduced CI noise. Replaced bash release hooks with a Go adapter for more reliable release automation and clearer failure modes.
